pageCache.text:
Situated in the heart of Gloucestershire, we are a friendly and caring school where children are encouraged to thrive, achieve and grow in confidence. We are committed to providing a rich and engaging education that helps every child develop academically, socially and emotionally.
At Dursley, we believe that every child has unique strengths and talents. Through high-quality teaching, exciting learning opportunities and strong relationships, we support all children to reach their full potential and become confident, responsible members of our community.
We invite you to explore our website to find out more about our wonderful school, our curriculum and the many opportunities available to our pupils. Our school is guided by our Christian values of Perseverance, Responsibility, Thankfulness, Forgiveness, Respect and Kindness, which help us to live out our vision:
“Together We Shine Brightly Because Together We Make A Difference”
Gloucestershire GL11 4NZ
The website is the hub for all news and events information.
If you would like any further information or to arrange a visit, please contact the school office.
admin@dursley.dgat.org.uk

Values
Dursley C of E Primary Academy has six important Christian Values: Respect, Responsibility, Thankfulness. Kindness, Forgiveness, Perseverance. Our pupils, parents and carers, Governors and staff were all involved in the creation of the values. These values are at the forefront of everything we do as a School Community.
We celebrate Values in action every week, during our celebration worship. The names of the pupils who have demonstrated the value, whether at home or school, are added to our Values Tree.
Worship
The school meets every day for collective worship, which, as the Education Act states, ‘is wholly or mainly of a broad Christian character, the main emphasis being on the broad traditions of Christian belief.”
Collective worship is an important and special part of our school day and reflects Church of England beliefs, practices and values in accordance with the requirements of the Trust Deed. Worship themes around our Christian values and are planned to support pupil’s spiritual development, to promote reflection on their own experiences and those of others and to learn about the life and teachings of Jesus.
Worship is led by the Head Teacher, members of the teaching staff, visiting clergy and the Open the Book Team. They are supported by members of the Reflect and Connect Pupil Parliament. We aim for our worship to be creative and inspirational by giving our pupils opportunities to listen to and act out stories, to listen to music and sing, pray and have time to reflect. From time to time worship takes place in the classroom and the children are given opportunities to reflect on our school Christian values. Pupils are encouraged, when appropriate, to help to plan and/or lead worship. This may take a variety of form, including being encouraged to ask and answer questions; act or mime a story; reading poems, prayers and stories; exploring artwork or leading the music/singing.
We are privileged to welcome pupils to our school from all faiths, none and from diverse cultures and lifestyles. Our collective worship is open to all, providing an opportunity to share in an experience which is emotional, reflective and invites the community to explore life through the lens of our vision and values. Pupils and adults are invited to engage in worship without compulsion and in a way that never compromises their integrity or dignity.
Spiritual Reflection
At Dursley CofE Primary Academy we believe that Spiritual Reflection offers a unique opportunity to step back and reflect on ourselves and the world in which we live. All schools have a responsibility to support their pupils’ spiritual development because the four Governments of the United Kingdom have each built this into their curriculum requirements and expectations.
We use the language of spirituality developed by the Education Department at the Diocese of Gloucester, the children are introduced to the concepts of wows, ows and nows. These are used to explore relationships with: ourselves, others, the wider natural world and beyond and offering the invitation to relate to God. Each classroom has a designated Spiritual Reflection area. Read about this here.

Our Vision
At Dursley C of E Primary Academy, we want every child to feel valued, supported and inspired to achieve their very best. Through an engaging and ambitious curriculum, we help our children develop the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to flourish both now and in the future.
We believe that strong relationships are at the heart of our school. By working together with families and the wider community, we create an environment where children feel safe, happy and ready to learn.
Together We Shine Brightly Because Together We Make A Difference
You are the light of the world. A town built on a hill cannot be hidden. Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a bowl. Instead they put it on its stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house. In the same way, let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in Heaven.

Our Curriculum
At Dursley C of E Primary Academy, we are passionate about valuing and nurturing every individual. Our inclusive, aspirational and inspiring curriculum enables the entire school community to flourish. We build supportive, trusting relationships rooted in mutual respect, creating happy, confident and active global citizens.
Together We Shine Brightly Because Together We Make A Difference
You are the light of the world. A town built on a hill cannot be hidden. Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a bowl. Instead they put it on its stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house. In the same way, let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in Heaven.
We have carefully developed our curriculum, which is based on the National Curriculum, to reflect our vision, through using three drivers, which are at the heart of all teaching and learning that takes place in our school. The curriculum drivers guide the development and delivery of that which is to be learning by the children at Dursley Primary, to enable everyone to ‘shine brightly’ and ‘make a difference’.

For more information about the club, please email :

Religious Education
Dursley C of E Primary Academy is a Church of England Academy and therefore Religious Education is provided in line with the funding agreement and the academy follows the Gloucestershire Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education 2025-2030.
​Religious Education enables all pupils to understand how religious and non-religious worldviews influence individuals, communities and society. The curriculum reflects the Gloucestershire Agreed Syllabus and supports pupils to think deeply, respond respectfully and develop spiritually. Curriculum Focus • Christianity taught in every key stage. • Judaism, Islam and Humanism in KS1. • Christianity, Islam, Hinduism and Judaism in KS2, with exploration of other worldviews. Our Approach RE is taught through three strands: Making Sense of Belief, Understanding the Impact and Making Connections. Lessons include explicit vocabulary, structured discussion, retrieval practice and reflective opportunities. Experiences Learning is enhanced through visits to places of worship, visitors from faith communities and thoughtful links to wider curriculum themes. Assessment and Impact Learning is assessed through end-of-unit tasks and ongoing teacher assessment. Pupils develop secure knowledge of beliefs, respectful understanding of diversity, the ability to reflect, and confidence to articulate thoughtful responses.

On track for excellence
At Dursley CE Primary Academy, we are committed to providing high-quality teaching that enables every child to flourish academically, socially and emotionally. Our Teaching and Learning Policy sets out the principles and approaches that underpin excellent classroom practice across the school.
Our curriculum is carefully planned to be ambitious, engaging and inclusive, ensuring that all children develop the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to succeed. Teachers use clear explanations, purposeful questioning, modelling, practice and feedback to support pupils in making strong progress. Through a consistent approach to teaching and learning, we create classrooms where children feel safe, valued and challenged.
We believe that every child can achieve. Guided by our vision, "Together we shine brightly and together we make a difference," we foster high expectations, positive relationships and a love of learning. Our teaching approaches are informed by educational research and are designed to help children become confident, independent and resilient learners.
Through effective teaching, strong relationships and a rich curriculum, we aim to ensure that every child leaves Dursley ready for the next stage of their educational journey and equipped to make a positive contribution to the world around them.

Curriculum Support at Home
At the start of every school year you are invited to an information session with your child’s class teacher where ideas will be shared.
Your child is expected to read at home everyday.
Your child will also be given homework.
The most important way you can help your child is to show an interest in what they do at school, ensure they attend regularly, eat a nutritious breakfast and get plenty of sleep.
You can really help your child by talking to them about what they have done at school but some children are more forthcoming than others.
To help you support your child, our curriculum pages have an overview of what your child will be learning each term as well as ideas to help specific to their class and topics.
We hold workshops throughout the year, sometimes by ages of children, where teachers tell you how we teach Maths and English. Additionally, we hold Family Fun sessions, which is an opportunity to engage in some learning and activities with your child within school.
Reading has astonishing benefits for children: comfort and reassurance, confidence and security, relaxation, happiness and fun. Giving a child time and full attention when reading them a story tells them they matter. It builds self-esteem, vocabulary, feeds imagination and even improves their sleeping patterns.

Beyond the classroom
At Dursley CofE Primary Academy, we offer extensive enrichment opportunities to all our pupils. These give children the chance to achieve, meet new people, try new activities and support their academic progress. The personal development of our pupils is at the forefront of our thinking, and we provide an extensive range of personal development opportunities including residential trips, day trips and visitors to the school. This not only supports the curriculum, but helps develop pupils’ talents and interests, to enable them to 'shine brightly' and 'make a difference'.
As part of our curriculum offer we provide all children with the opportunity to learn outdoors through our Forest School Provision. We feel Forest School helps our children to develop socially, emotionally, spiritually, physically and intellectually. It creates a safe, non-judgmental nurturing environment for our children to try news things and take risks.
We have three Pupil Parliaments at Dursley CofE Primary Academy. These actively promote pupil leadership opportunities, enabling the children to develop valuable communication, co-operation, organisational and debating skills, as well as developing a sense of responsibility and deepening their understanding of democracy.
Our school offers a range of clubs: from golf to drawing and choir to gardening. We strive to provide an ever-changing range of clubs so that all pupils have an opportunity to attend a club that interests them – and we are always looking for new ideas.

Our Pupil Parliament
At Dursley C of E Primary Academy, we believe that every child should have a voice and the opportunity to help shape our school. Our Pupil Parliament gives children the chance to represent their classmates, share ideas and work together to make a positive difference across the academy.
Our Pupil Parliament plays an important role in ensuring that pupils are involved in decisions that affect school life. By listening to the views of others and working collaboratively, our representatives help make our school an even better place to learn and grow.
Our Worship Team
Our Worship Team plays an important role in helping to shape and lead our collective worship. Made up of enthusiastic pupils from across the school, the team works alongside staff to ensure worship is engaging, meaningful and reflective of our Christian vision and values.
The Worship Team helps to plan worship themes, lead prayers, gather pupil voice and contribute ideas that support the spiritual life of our school. They encourage others to reflect on our vision, "Together We Shine Brightly Because Together We Make a Difference," and help create opportunities for everyone to participate in worship.
Our Together Committee
The Together Committee is a group of pupils who are passionate about helping others and strengthening our school community. Inspired by our vision, "Together We Shine Brightly Because Together We Make a Difference," the committee works to promote inclusion, wellbeing and positive relationships throughout the academy.
As agents of change, members of the Together Committee identify opportunities to improve school life, listen to the views of their peers and take positive action to make a difference. They help to ensure that every child feels heard, valued and included, while encouraging a culture of kindness, belonging and mutual support.
The committee leads and supports a range of initiatives, including community projects, charitable events, wellbeing activities and campaigns that have a positive impact both within school and beyond. Through their work, pupils learn that even small actions can create meaningful change.

Attendance
For a brief overview on how you can help you child achieve good attendance, please have a look at our attendance guidance:
The children at Dursley C of E Primary Academy enjoy learning and want to be in school. Good attendance is key to learning and development and we expect you to make sure that your child attends school regularly and on time.
Our school gates are opened at 8.30am. Children and parents/carers should wait in the playground until the doors are opened at 8.40am. The school day starts at 845am. The gates will then be locked at 8.55am. The parent of any child arriving at school after 8.55am will need to go to the school office.
Any child arriving at school after 9.15am will be marked in the register with a ‘Late’ mark. A letter will be sent to parents if there is a pattern of persistent lateness. If a child arrives after 9.15am an unauthorised absence code (U) will be used, unless the school office have been informed of a medical appointment.
If you experience any difficulty in getting your child to school on time it is really important that you speak to your class teacher or the school office as soon as possible.
Leave of absence will not be authorised in term time unless there are exceptional circumstances. In this instance you must request authorised leave from the Head Teacher, Mrs Heather Gregory.
If you intend taking your child out of school it is essential that you complete a Leave of Absence Form at least two weeks before the intended absence so that we know that your child is absent from school and in your care. This is required irrespective of whether the absence will be authorised or unauthorised.
REPORTING ABSENCE
We do understand that sometimes children are ill or have to attend medical appointments.
If your child is ill, we ask that you telephone the school by 8.45am on the first day of absence (01453 542304) and leave your child’s name, class and reason for absence. If your child is likely to absent from school for a longer period of time we ask that you keep us updated with the likely date of return, but it is not necessary to phone each day.
If you are unsure about your child’s illness and their attendance at school, here is a useful link: https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/is-my-child-too-ill-for-school/
If your child has a medical appointment, please could you inform the school office and provide a copy of the appointment letter or text. The office staff will make sure that your child’s absence is correctly recorded in the register and that the class teacher is made aware.

Healthy School
At Dursley CE Primary Academy, we are committed to helping our children develop healthy habits that support their wellbeing, learning and long-term health. Through our curriculum, physical activity opportunities, healthy eating initiatives and wellbeing support, we encourage children to make positive choices and understand the importance of looking after both their physical and mental health.
As part of this commitment, we are proud to be a nut-free school. This is an important measure to help keep members of our school community safe, particularly those with severe nut allergies. We therefore ask all families to ensure that packed lunches, snacks and food brought into school do not contain nuts or nut-based products.
We also promote healthy eating through our approach to packed lunches and snacks. We encourage a balanced lunch containing items such as sandwiches, fruit, vegetables, yoghurt and other nutritious options. Sweets and confectionery are not permitted, and whilst small nut-free lunchbox chocolate snacks may be included occasionally, full-size chocolate bars are not allowed.
By working together, we can help every child develop healthy habits and ensure that our school remains a safe, inclusive and supportive environment where all children can flourish.
School dinners
At Dursley CE Primary Academy, we believe that healthy, nutritious meals play an important role in supporting children’s wellbeing, concentration and readiness to learn.
Our school meals are freshly prepared and cooked on site each day in our school kitchen, ensuring that children enjoy high-quality, balanced meals made with care. We work in partnership with Caterlink, who provide a varied menu designed to meet nutritional standards while offering children a choice of delicious and enjoyable meals.
Our menus are regularly updated to reflect seasonal ingredients and provide a range of options to suit different tastes and dietary requirements.
You can view copies of the current Caterlink menus below to see the meals available to your child.
Snack time
At Dursley CE Primary Academy, we encourage all children to make healthy choices that support their wellbeing, learning and concentration throughout the school day.
Children in Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and Key Stage 1 are provided with a piece of fruit each day as part of the government's School Fruit and Vegetable Scheme.Children in Key Stage 2 are invited to bring a snack from home to enjoy at morning break time.
We ask families to choose healthy snack options, such as:
Other healthy, low-sugar snacks
To support our Healthy Schools approach, chocolate, sweets, confectionery and other sweet treats are not permitted as break-time snacks.
These items should not be brought into school for morning break.As a nut-free school, all snacks brought from home must also be free from nuts and nut-based products to help keep all members of our school community safe.
